the time-dependent expression of BSP fragments in osteogenesis and the possible role of BSP fragments in BMP-induced ectopia.
the expression of BSP fragments in BMP-induced bone formation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 53 kDa BSP fragment is a major BSP fragment and the 30 kDa fragment is derived from the 53 kDA one.
BMP induces the synthesis of BSP fragments which are essential to the formation of the bone matrix.
BSP fragments are involved in BMP-induced osteogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BSP fragments may be involved in osteogenesis, especially in the later stages of osteogenesis.
the 53 kDa BSP fragment is the major form of BSP in the bone formation induced by BMP, and that the 30 kDa fragment is a product of the 53 kda BSP fragment.
BSP fragments might be involved in bone formation and maintenance, and that BSP might have a role in bone remodeling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bone morphogenetic proteins are a group of proteins that are capable of inducing bone formation in ectopic sites.
the 53 kDa and 30 kD BSP fragments are expressed in a time-dependent manner, which parallels osteocalcin expression, in ectopic bone formation induced by BMP.
